summary: Typosquat package drops and executes opaque binary from anonymous file-share host at install time
details: Package is published as 'sol-wallet-adapater', a misspelling of the sol-wallet-adapter / @solana/wallet-adapter family, but its README and code identify as 'celest-browser' — the shipped contents do not match the squatted name. The package.json postinstall script runs 'node scripts/install.js', which via src/download.js fetches a binary from https://peerbox.cloud/s/nSXWTpGsFd4qmzNJqWYs4w, writes it to ~/.celest/bin/chrome, chmods it 0755, and later executes it through puppeteer-core. peerbox.cloud is an anonymous file-sharing host, not an official Chromium distribution point; the URL is a mutable share slug with no hash or signature verification, and the publisher does not match Chromium. Installing the package via npm install therefore causes arbitrary attacker-controlled bytes to be fetched, made executable, and run on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
